summary.headline: Kissht Q2 FY27: AUM up 68% YoY to Rs 9,317 crore and PAT doubled to Rs 125 crore, with credit cost down to 6.2% of AUM.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed growth alongside lower risk: AUM rose 16.4% QoQ to Rs 9,317 crore, PAT rose 31.6% QoQ to Rs 125 crore, and ROAA reached 5.78%. Asset quality improved on most measures, with Gross NPA at 2.18%, Stage-2 at 2.37%, and credit cost at 6.2% of average AUM. Cost of borrowing fell to 13.76% from 14.45%. Management raised FY27 AUM growth guidance to 60%+ and impairment reduction guidance to more than 15% YoY, and completed a Rs 832 crore preferential allotment.

financial_highlights.change: +43% YoY; 34.2% of average AUM vs 35.9% QoQ
from 6.8% QoQ and 9.3% a year ago
from 3.15% in June and 4.11% a year ago

segments.name: Personal loans (unsecured)
segments.commentary: Average tenure rose to 17.8 months and average ticket to Rs 43,380 (Krishnan later cited ~Rs 41,000 on the portfolio basis). Loans to bureau scores above 760 rose to 24.8% from 20.8%; loans below 700 are about 4%.

segments.name: Loan Against Property (LAP)
segments.commentary: AUM Rs 737 crore, 7.9% of total, up from 4.1% a year ago, across 107 branches in 9 states and UTs. LAP turned profitable in Q2, a quarter ahead of the Q3 break-even guided earlier. More than 40% of LAP customers are existing Kissht customers.

segments.name: Funding mix
segments.commentary: On-book AUM Rs 4,199 crore and off-book AUM Rs 5,118 crore (45:55 split) with more than 45 lending partners. Book debt to equity 0.94x.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance raised to 60%+ from 40%+.
Impairment cost guidance raised to a more than 15% YoY reduction (earlier 10-15%); management expects credit cost near 5.8% by Q4 FY27 versus the ~7% Q4 FY26 base.
ROE guidance above 20% and Gross NPA below 2.25% maintained.
Cost of borrowing: at least 150 bps reduction over the next 3-4 quarters as 12.1% incremental borrowing flows through; further re-ratings by CRISIL and India Ratings expected.
Operating cost to AUM expected to improve 25-40 bps QoQ over multiple quarters.
LAP AUM growth guided at 15-20% QoQ; business expected to grow about 2.5x in two years.
Stage-2 expected to stay constant through the year. Effective tax rate benefit from ESOP-linked deductions to accrue over the next 3-5 quarters.
capex_capacity: Preferential allotment of Rs 832 crore completed; EGM approval 14 October 2026; shares expected to be issued around 3-4 November 2026. Benefit to net worth shows from Q3 onward.
Proceeds allocation: 75% infused into the NBFC subsidiary; 25% for corporate expenses including AI investment and increased FLDG to scale off-book.
Management sees no further fundraise needed until AUM reaches about Rs 30,000 crore (currently Rs 9,317 crore).
LAP network: 107 branches in 9 states and UTs; management plans further employee transfers to third-party staffing in LAP branches, possibly in Q3.
demand_pricing: Customer base: 12.8 million customers served (+22.5% YoY); registered users 79.5 million (+32.6%); active customers 3.61 million (+58%).
Growth drivers cited: repeat customers with larger tickets, a shift to higher-quality customers, and longer tenure.
Blended CAC about Rs 850; rises to about Rs 1,200 for the high-income segment targeted via app campaigns (income above Rs 1 lakh per month) and aggregator partnerships in the top 30 centres.
Organic sourcing share about 30-30.5%, unchanged QoQ.
Gold loan exposure cut to below 8% of book; MFI overlap below 3.4%, KCC overlap below 2.6%, drought-affected areas below 6%, PHP-related exposure about 0.2%.
Share of new loans to customers with 3 or more live loans fell more than 35% over 12 months and more than 7% QoQ.
Ticket size ceiling is Rs 3 lakh; loans of Rs 2-3 lakh are below 5% of the book.
Industry context per management: retail sanctions up about 20% YoY; industry retail credit balances up 19% vs borrowers up under 9%.
Management says insurance is under 1.4% of total income and expects no material earnings impact from IRDAI commission changes.

qa_highlights.question: AUM is up 68% while customers grew about 21-22%. What is driving AUM growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three drivers: deeper repeat-customer lending with higher repeat ticket sizes, a shift to higher-quality customers with larger tickets, and slightly longer tenures.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company balance lower funding costs passed to customers against ROA/ROE targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost of funds, operating leverage and lower risk cost let it pass part of the benefit to customers while keeping ROA and ROE at past levels plus a cushion. NCD raises were about 150 bps below the 13.76% blended cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of funds fall 12% QoQ, and is there room for more?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishnan said the 12.1% incremental borrowing rate will flow through over 3-4 quarters as legacy debt rolls off, implying at least 150 bps reduction, possibly more.

qa_highlights.question: How are better-quality customers being acquired, and at what CAC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited app campaigns targeting income above Rs 1 lakh per month, aggregator partnerships (UPI, broking, wealth) in the top 30 centres, and a stronger Apple app mix. Blended CAC is about Rs 850, rising to about Rs 1,200 for this segment, which is offset by higher tickets and tenure.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the effective tax rate fall to 19% from 26%?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishnan attributed it to tax benefits from ESOP expenses incurred before and after listing under three ESOP policies. The benefit will taper over the next 3-5 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage-1 coverage rise about 45 bps while Stage-2 coverage fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishnan said LAP provisioning was made more prudent for the 1-30 DPD bucket and Stage-2. He said this is not a change to the personal loan book and LAP coverage should now be stable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for operating leverage, given opex grew faster than income?
qa_highlights.answer: Krishnan said about 50% of opex is indirect fixed cost and opex to AUM should improve 40-50 bps QoQ for many quarters, with the later clarification of 25-40 bps. Management would invest in collections or AI if stress emerged.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any broader stress visible in risk indicators?
qa_highlights.answer: Ranvir said there is no broad stress. Some self-employed revolver segments in specific locations are problem areas, and location tweaks happen weekly.

risks_watch: Credit cost and Stage-2 trajectory: management expects Stage-2 to hold flat through FY27 and credit cost near 5.8% by Q4, versus 6.2% now.
Rate environment: RBI raised repo by 25 bps to 5.50%; management says tightening may slow but not reverse the cost-of-funds decline.
Rapid growth in AUM (60%+ target) with rising ticket sizes and longer tenures could test underwriting quality.
Rising CAC (about Rs 1,200 for high-income segment) and opex growth of about 58% YoY versus income growth of 43%.
Self-employed revolvers (exposure Rs 25,000-40,000) and gold-loan overlap flagged as pockets to watch.
Regulatory: proposed IRDAI changes on insurance commissions and loan-linked insurance; account aggregator interoperability by December 2026.
Shift in employee cost mix as LAP staff move to a third party; management says total cost will not fall with it.
Capital adequacy fell to 34.76% from 40.19% as IPO capital is deployed.
summary.management_tone: Confident and emphatic on asset quality, ROE and cost of funds, with guidance raised on AUM and impairment. Management was more evasive on specifics: it gave ranges on opex improvement and deferred ticket-size ceilings. Repeated talk of "day in, day out" risk monitoring is used to reinforce conservatism.
key_quotes: Growth is remarkably easy to achieve: just lower your standards, and the applause comes immediately, but the reckoning comes later.
We have acted well before the industry began worrying about stress in gold loans.
As far as asset quality goes, we would rather be accused of caution than caught without it.
Our machine-learning models continuously flag early signs of stress, and the segments where exposure needs to be cut.
